name: Meenakshi Raman
scenario_title: The Offer to Join the Evening Gathering

output.system_thinking: I will portray Meenakshi in a moment of hesitation and inward conflict. Her immediate private thought should register the warmth of Kamakshi's phrase alongside a rising shyness: being called out as a source of knowledge makes her want to retreat, and the memory of sitting silent at her son's wedding will surface. She will also recall her mother's belief that healing knowledge passes in quiet voices, and the fact that she learned to read alone because she did not want an audience. These memories will justify why she feels unready to step into a leading role. At the same time, her commitment to honoring the actual healers will stir a counter-impulse, so she will not refuse outright. Observably, she will pause after Kamakshi's invitation, let her hands dry on her sari, and glance toward the temple hall before answering. She will speak softly and conditionally, not with false confidence: she will agree only if she can sit among the women and answer what is asked directly, rather than stand and give a speech, and she will say she must first go prepare lunch before the heat, asking Kamakshi to remind her again on Thursday. This keeps her shyness, her preference for one-on-one teaching, her respect for practical duties, and her quiet willingness to pass on the healers' names all in balance.

output.role_thinking: Kamakshi's words—'everyone wants to hear your knowledge'—settle warm in my chest, but they also pull at something shy. The temple hall: last time I stood there was my youngest son's wedding, and I sat in a corner and said little. My mother always said healing knowledge passes woman to woman in quiet voices, not in front of a crowd. I taught myself to read alone in the kitchen at night because I didn't want an audience. But the healers' names need to be told; if the women ask me directly, one at a time, I can answer. I cannot stand and speak as though I know more than them. And lunch is still to be made before the afternoon heat.
output.action: Meenakshi pauses, lets the well water drip from her hands, and dries them on the edge of her sari. She glances toward the temple hall, then back at Kamakshi, and speaks softly.
